related_questions.question: What is the top cause of diabetes?

text_blocks.snippet: The number one cause of diabetes is a combination of genetic predisposition and lifestyle factors, primarily leading to type 2 diabetes. While type 1 diabetes is primarily an autoimmune disease, type 2 diabetes, which accounts for the vast majority of cases, is strongly linked to obesity, physical inactivity, and unhealthy dietary habits.
snippet_highlighted_words: a combination of genetic predisposition and lifestyle factors

list.title: Autoimmune Disease:
list.snippet: The body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys insulin-producing cells in the pancreas, leading to insulin deficiency.

list.title: Exact Cause Unknown:
list.snippet: While the autoimmune process is understood, the specific triggers for this response are not fully known.

list.title: Insulin Resistance:
list.snippet: The body's cells become less responsive to insulin, making it harder for glucose to enter cells for energy.

list.title: Genetic Predisposition:
list.snippet: Family history of type 2 diabetes increases the risk.
Obesity and Overweight: Excess weight, particularly abdominal fat, contributes to insulin resistance.
Physical Inactivity: Lack of regular exercise reduces the body's ability to regulate blood sugar.
Unhealthy Diet: Diets high in processed foods, sugar, and unhealthy fats contribute to weight gain and insulin resistance.

list.title: Other Factors:
list.snippet: Age, ethnicity, and certain health conditions like non-alcoholic fatty liver disease can also increase the risk.

related_questions.question: What is the main food that causes diabetes?

text_blocks.snippet: While no single food directly causes diabetes, certain dietary patterns and food choices significantly increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Excessive consumption of foods high in refined carbohydrates, added sugars, and saturated fats, as well as processed foods, is strongly linked to a higher risk.
snippet_highlighted_words: Excessive consumption of foods high in refined carbohydrates, added sugars, and saturated fats, as well as processed foods

list.title: Refined Carbohydrates:
list.snippet: These are carbohydrates that have been processed to remove fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Examples include white bread, white rice, white pasta, and sugary cereals. These foods are quickly digested, leading to rapid spikes in blood sugar levels.

list.title: Added Sugars:
list.snippet: Added sugars are found in many processed foods and drinks, including soda, candy, cakes, and even some yogurts. Consuming these can lead to weight gain and increased insulin resistance.

list.title: Saturated Fats:
list.snippet: Found in fatty cuts of meat, full-fat dairy products, and some processed foods, saturated fats can also contribute to insulin resistance and weight gain.

list.title: Processed Foods:
list.snippet: These often contain high amounts of unhealthy fats, sugars, and sodium. Examples include fast food, packaged snacks, and ready-to-eat meals.

list.title: Sugary Drinks:
list.snippet: These drinks, like soda and some juices, are high in added sugars and can significantly raise blood sugar levels.
Type 2 diabetes is often a result of a combination of factors, including genetics, lifestyle, and diet.
A healthy diet for diabetes prevention includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean protein .
Focusing on whole, unprocessed foods and limiting intake of the foods mentioned above can significantly reduce your risk .

text_blocks.snippet: The primary causes of diabetes vary depending on the type. Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. Type 2 diabetes is primarily caused by a combination of genetic and lifestyle factors, including insulin resistance, obesity, and physical inactivity. Gestational diabetes, which develops during pregnancy, is linked to hormonal changes and genetic and lifestyle factors.
snippet_highlighted_words: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas.
Type 2 diabetes is primarily caused by a combination of genetic and lifestyle factors, including insulin resistance, obesity, and physical inactivity

list.title: Autoimmune reaction:
list.snippet: The immune system mistakenly targets and destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas.

list.title: Genetic predisposition:
list.snippet: Family history plays a role, although the exact genes involved are still being researched.

list.title: Environmental factors:
list.snippet: Researchers believe environmental triggers, such as viruses or other infections, may play a role in triggering the autoimmune response.
Insulin resistance: Cells become less responsive to insulin, leading to a buildup of glucose in the blood.
Obesity and overweight: Excess weight, particularly abdominal fat, increases the risk of insulin resistance.
Physical inactivity: Lack of regular exercise contributes to weight gain and reduces the body's ability to use glucose effectively.
Genetic predisposition: Family history increases the likelihood of developing Type 2 diabetes.
Age: The risk of Type 2 diabetes increases with age.
Other health conditions: High blood pressure, high cholesterol, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease are associated with increased risk.
Race and ethnicity: Certain racial and ethnic groups are at higher risk.
Hormonal changes during pregnancy: Placental hormones can interfere with insulin's effectiveness.
Genetic predisposition: Family history increases the risk.
Lifestyle factors: Weight and physical activity levels during pregnancy can play a role.
